text: The model looks at three key pieces of the applicant’s credit picture. First, the revolving‑credit utilization is very high (about 89 % of the available credit is being used). This pushes the risk score upward, because using a large share of credit lines is usually a warning sign. Second, the debt‑to‑income figure is low (the applicant’s debt is only a small portion of their income). That pulls the risk score down, indicating the borrower has enough income to cover their obligations. Finally, the applicant has no recent 30‑ to 59‑day past‑due accounts, which also lowers the risk. When the strong, low‑risk signals from income and payment history are combined with the single high‑utilization signal, the overall assessment comes out as “low risk.”
